text:
Wind worried the open greenhouse door while rain began ticking against the glass. Selin stood at the entrance, staring at her notebook on the floor beyond the crowded rows. She took one step forward, then stopped. The direct way was too narrow to pass without brushing against the plants.

“I can get it myself,” she said.

Bora glanced toward the clear side path. He waited.

Another gust swept through the doorway. The notebook’s paper cover fluttered, and Selin’s stubbornness finally gave way.

“Bora, will you help me reach my notebook?”

He looked at her, clearly hearing the request, then nodded. “Come around this side.”

Bora led her along the greenhouse side path and held the open door steady against the wind. From there, Selin could move between the rows without crowding the plants. Bora stayed by the door, keeping it from swinging into her as she hurried across the floor.

Selin crouched and closed both hands around her original notebook. Bora watched her lift it safely against her chest.

“Got it,” she said, letting out a breath.

Rain drummed harder overhead. Selin returned along the side path. When she reached Bora, she did not push past him or pretend she had managed alone. She paused, met his eyes, and held the door for him in return.

“Your way worked,” she said. “Thanks.”

Bora gave a small smile and stepped through. Selin followed, tucking the notebook securely beneath her jacket. Together they hurried back into the school courtyard as the rain strengthened, no longer arguing over who had solved the problem.
